I see you already saw the small discussion from yesterday, and while I don't want to end up as a one-trick pony touting one series, let me add some more points:

  • It's as hard as sci fi gets. No FTL, no aliens, lots of descriptions of how dust fucks up your day. KSR knows Mars as well as his own back yard, and if you take no pleasure from a detailed breakdown of geology or how the changed atmosphere affects sunsets, you will fall asleep plenty.
  • It is a tour de force in future history, with a fairly plausible and well-developed scenario for Mars-Earth relations as well as Red/Green factions on Mars herself.
  • Agreed on the audiobook, it is monotone and dreary.
  • Most readers seem to prefer Red over Green over Blue; the story expands in time and space and scope and does perhaps drag on a bit.
  • KSR is not known for creating the deepest characters. I'd argue that the Mars Trilogy is better than most of his works, but the planet itself is the main character in these books, and technology and politics also trump any interpersonal stories told.
  • You will learn more about the planet than you ever thought possible, and to this day I still can look at a map and think there's Underhill, there's Burroughs, Hiroko's hideout, Sheffield with the space elevator, oh I wish I could hike Noctis Labyrinthus with Coyote...

Pinterest is a good place to look for tips! We've been wanting to bring our 18 month old soon and we've been researching :)

We started with our kids (campgrounds...not backcountry) when they were 9 months and 2 years old. A portable playpen helped with the 9 month old...she managed to find all the wrong things to stick on her mouth. :)

Always remember their bedtimes and scheduled....and even if the days are longer, do your campfire early to make sure you can pack them off to bed at a reasonable time. I think a lot of parents push the little ones a bit too hard. Mind you, we also had to drive ours around on a couple of occasions to get them to fall asleep in the car.

Oh...and using the laundry tubs to wash them down seem to work better than getting them in the campground showers. Something about the shower stalls terrified them.

And finally....bring something for allergies. It's amazing how differently a little 2 year old body reacts to a bunch of mosquito bites compared to an older one.

It was a lot of work, but man, did it pay off. My kids are in their 20's now and still look forward to camping trips. We had a ton of fun all through the years. God for you for starting them off early!

My young kids love to play in the sand and rocks when we go camping (9 and 4). When younger we had a playpen with a mosquito net over top and after that we had a tend with screen around it that would normally go over a table. An epi-pen is a great thing for your first aid kit, and lots and lots of baby wipes.
